sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice E.V.Venugopal
 Criminal Petition No.13205 Of 2024

This criminal petition is filed by the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 14 under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)
seeking to quash the proceedings in CC No.420 of 2024, on the file of the learned Judicial First Class Magistrate at Korutla, Jagtial District.
2. Heard K.Venumadhav, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State/1st respondent.

3. CC No.420 of 2024 on the file of the trial Court is registered basing on the complainant lodged by the 2nd respondent dated 11.01.2023 that having not satisfied with the amount given towards dowry and other gifts, her husband, his parents, sisters and brothers- in-law harassed the de-facto complainant mentally and physically demanding additional dowry, unable to bear with such harassment, the de-facto complainant got registered Crime No.205 of 2016 of PS, Korutla for the offences under Section 498-A IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of DP Act and started living with her parents.
To her shock and surprise, the second marriage of the 1st accused was performed with the 2nd accused during subsistence of the marriage between the de-facto complainant and the 1st accused.

Accordingly, a crime in FIR No.85 o 2023 of PS, Korutla for the offence under Section 494 read with Section 34 of IPC was registered and after completion of investigation, a charge-sheet was laid and the same was numbered as CC No.420 of 2024 on the file of the learned Judicial First Class Magistrate at Korutla, Jagtial District against the petitioners/accused.

4. Aggrieved by the same, the petitioners filed the present criminal petition mainly contending that the allegations levelled against them in the charge-sheet are baseless and they do not constitute any offence much less the alleged offence against them and that as per Section 198 of Cr.P.C. no Court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under Chapter XX of the Indian Penal Code and that since Section 494 IPC comes under the said Chapter, the trial Court cannot take cognizance of the same.

The said contention finds support from the findings of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Mamidala Ramesh Vs. State, Station House Officer, represented by Public Prosecutor, High Court of Andhra Pradesh 1.
5.

This Court heard the submissions made on either side, the decision relied upon on behalf of the petitioners and perused the material on record.

7. In the case of Mamidala Ramesh (cited supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has categorically held that Section 494 IPC falls under Chapter XX of Indian Penal Code dealing with the offences relating to marriage.

Relying upon the decisions rendered in K.Vijaya Lakshmi Vs.K.Lakshminarayana 2 and Vijaya Lakshmi Vs. Sanjeev Reddy 3 the Hon'ble Apex Court in the above referred decision further held that in view of the bar imposed by Section 198 of the Code, the Magistrate had no power to take cognizance of an offence under Section 494 IPC based on a police report.

8. Section 494 IPC does not extend to any person whose marriage with such husband or wife has been declared void by a Court of competent jurisdiction, nor to any person who contracts a marriage during the life of a former husband or wife, if such husband or wife, at the time of the subsequent marriage, shall have been continually absent from such person for the space of seven years, and shall not have been heard of by such person as being alive within that time provided the person contracting such subsequent marriage shall, before such marriage takes place, inform the person with whom such marriage is 2000(2) ALD (Crl.) 184 2000(2) ALD (Crl.) 200 contracted of the real state of facts so far as the same are within his or her knowledge.

9. When the facts of the case on hand are observed, admittedly, the marriage of the de-facto complainant and the 1st petitioner/accused was performed 18 years back and after four years of their marriage, alleging that the 1st petitioner and his other family members started harassing the de-facto complainant, she apart from initiating criminal proceedings under Section 498A IPC,
started living with her parents, separately away from the 1st petitioner/husband and hence, the bar under Section 198 of Cr.P.C. clearly hits the present proceedings and hence, taking cognizance of the charge-sheet by the learned Judge of the trial Court is bad in law and accordingly, the present criminal proceedings are liable to be quashed against the petitioners herein.
10.

In the result, this criminal petition is allowed quashing the proceedings against the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 14 in CC No.420 of 2024, on the file of the learned Judicial First Class Magistrate at Korutla, Jagtial District.
